content:
Apple is set to report its fiscal third-quarter results for 2026, followed by what will be the final earnings call hosted by Tim Cook as the company's CEO. Here's how to tune in live.

Ongoing component shortages are expected to once again play a significant role.

Half an hour after the market close, Apple will release its fiscal third-quarter results for 2026, followed by an earnings call hosted by CEO Tim Cook and CFO Kevan Parekh. This will mark Tim Cook's final appearance on an earnings call as Apple's CEO, and his 90th earnings call overall.

During the previous quarter's call, incoming CEO John Ternus made a brief appearance to thank Cook, Apple's management team, employees, and long-term shareholders, while expressing optimism about the company's future.

Last quarter, Apple projected year-over-year revenue growth between 14% and 17%, with gross margins between 47.5% and 48.5%. This translates to expected revenue of approximately $107.2 billion to $110 billion, against a Wall Street consensus of around $109 billion.

Apple is expected to address the impact of ongoing component shortages, its recent price increases, and its outlook on future demand during the earnings call.

Apple's earnings call will begin at 2:00 p.m. Pacific Time / 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time, with management delivering prepared remarks before transitioning to analyst questions.

As always, the call will be live-streamed, and you can listen in via this link.

Stay tuned to 9to5Mac later today for comprehensive coverage of Apple's Q3 2026 results, including highlights from the earnings call.
